summary: Round-3 confirming pass. The sampler hardening is correct and closes the silent-green the round-2 reviewers measured: countFiles is retried 3x, a final failure is recorded rather than thrown, the whole loop is wrapped in catch(Throwable), and the last-sample-within-5s assertion catches a death that records nothing. Verified by extracting the round-2 approved file from the r2 packet and diffing: the delta touches only the sampler block, the two comment corrections and the backlog row -- the per-window cadence loop, the measured 2.0 threshold, the warm-up probe and the whole of http/build.gradle.kts are byte-identical to what round 2 approved. No src/main path is staged; no object-store request rate is affected by this commit. Three minors, all in the round-3 prose delta, none blocking; per review.md rule 11 they belong in the commit body, not in a round 4.

findings.title: The round-3 '~152 -> ~166 files' correction was applied to one of the two places the identical sentence appears, and the number it introduced does not reconcile with the commit's own measurements
findings.detail: The same claim is written verbatim in two places: 'so ~166 files are written either way and only elapsed time differs' (backlog M3.5 row) and 'so the same ~152 files are written either way and only the elapsed time differs' (test comment, line 350). Diffing the round-2 packet against this one shows all three occurrences read ~152 at the reviewed hash 5c8b2ad8; round 3 changed the two backlog occurrences and left the test file's. Both numbers cannot be right, and the arithmetic favours the one that was left behind: 200 MB / 24 producers = 8.74 MB each, at ~230 B/record that is ~37,992 records = 38 blocking 1000-record chunks, so 38 flushes x 4 files (segment + delta, each with its .v sidecar, per the countFiles javadoc at line 144) = ~152. The commit's own recorded clean-path measurement agrees: 182 windows at a median 0.790 files/s over ~192s of load is ~152 files. 166 is not a multiple of the 4-files-per-flush unit this comment block is built on (166/4 = 41.5); it is close to 152 + the 12 files the three warm-up flushes write, which is a different quantity from the one the sentence is about.
findings.failure_scenario: A future agent sizing or re-deriving the 2.0 files/s threshold reads backlog.md as the durable record, computes ~166 files over the ~192s load = 0.86 files/s, and concludes the clean-path margin is 2.3x rather than the 2.5x the test comment states -- or, reading both, cannot tell which of the two numbers in the same commit was measured and which was guessed, which is exactly the state non-negotiable 4 exists to prevent. Record it in the commit body; the honest resolution at the milestone boundary (rule 13) is to restore ~152 in the backlog, not to change the test file.
findings.recommendation: Record as a minor in the commit body. Do not open a round 4 for it.

findings.title: The replacement sensitivity gloss is as unsupported as the one it replaced, in the opposite direction
findings.detail: The derived half of the new sentence is right and I checked it: with the ceiling at 0.79 files/s and the floor regime at 4.33 files/s, a 10s window needs f seconds of floor to reach 20 files, 7.9 + 3.54f > 20, f > 3.42 -- so '~3.4s of floor regime inside its 10s' is correct and is on its own a complete statement of the sensitivity. The clause that follows it, 'so a floor stretch confined to roughly the last 5% of the body would still slip through', is a second, unmeasured unit conversion. By time, 3.4s of a ~192s load is ~1.8%. By bytes, using the mutated run's own figures recorded three lines above (66s total with ~77% of 200 MB through the floor regime, i.e. ~7 MB/s at the floor), 3.4s is ~24 MB, ~12%. Neither is 5%. Round 2 filed the previous version of this same sentence ('catches that at the first floor-regime second') for overstating sensitivity ~3.5x; the replacement understates the hole by a similar factor in bytes while overstating it in time, so the correction did not settle the number, it moved it.
findings.failure_scenario: A later change that shortens the interval only over the tail of the load -- the realistic shape, since adaptInterval's shorten branch is one-way -- is sized against '5% of the body' and assumed to be caught, when by the comment's own byte arithmetic a stretch up to ~12% of the body slips through. The safe reading is the derived one (~3.4s), and the byte gloss should either be dropped or carry the floor throughput it was computed from.
findings.recommendation: Record as a minor. If ever touched, delete the '~5% of the body' clause and keep the ~3.4s figure, which is derivable from numbers already in the comment.

findings.title: The whole sampler race exists only because the cadence is measured by walking the filesystem, where CountingBinStore already exists to count requests
findings.detail: binstore-spi/src/main/java/binjava/binstore/CountingBinStore.java is the project's own decorator for exactly this job ('Counts every request a delegate issues (cost rule R9)'), it is public in binjava.binstore, it reaches this test's classpath transitively through http's api(project(":ingest")) -> api(project(":binstore-spi")), and M3.4's IntervalPutRateTest already uses it to assert a PUT rate. Wrapping the store here -- new DefaultIngest(config, new CountingBinStore(new LocalFsBinStore(root)), ...) and sampling counting.counts().puts() -- would read an atomic LongAdder instead of doing a Files.walk of a growing directory once per second. That single substitution deletes the race the round-2 reviewers found, and with it the retry loop, the samplerFailures list, the catch(Throwable), the last-sample assertion and roughly 30 lines of comment justifying them -- the entire round-3 delta. It would also express the assertion in PUT/s, the unit ADR-0016's table and non-negotiable 6 are written in, instead of a files/s proxy that conflates two objects per flush, two files per object, and the transient put*.tmp that countFiles also counts. I am filing this as minor rather than major deliberately: the test as staged works and was demonstrated to kill the mutation it was built for, and forcing a round 4 to rewrite the sampler would restart the exact spiral rule 12 was measured on.
findings.failure_scenario: As staged the cadence signal is a file count that includes .v sidecars and transient put*.tmp files, so it drifts by +/-1 per sample and must carry 2.5x margin to stay quiet; and any future backend or LocalFsBinStore change to the tmp/rename dance reopens a sampler race that has now been papered over twice. A PUT counter cannot drift, cannot throw, and cannot die.
findings.recommendation: Record as a minor now; make it a backlog row for the next time this test is touched, alongside M0.52.

process_judgement.question: Was exceeding review.md rule 12's 2-round cap justified?
process_judgement.answer: Partly, and the author cited the wrong rule. Round 2 returned pass from both reviewers, so rule 12 was never engaged -- rule 12 governs a BLOCKING finding in round two ('does not buy a round three -- it means the commit is too big'). What round 2 produced was a pass carrying a minor, which is rule 11: fixing it is 'permitted and usually wrong'. So the question is not whether a cap was broken but whether the fix was worth a round. For items 1-3, the sampler hardening: yes, and I would have made the same call. A 1-in-200-to-400 chance that the only proof of NFR-6 at the interval's ceiling reports green having measured a prefix is not a prose minor -- it is the failure mode non-negotiable 4 rests on, and it was introduced BY the round-2 fix, so nobody had yet had the chance to record it as pre-existing. For item 4, the three comment/number corrections: no. Those are textbook rule-11 minors, they were bundled into the same round for convenience, and rule 11's stated failure mode -- 'the next round's surface is the prose the fix just added' -- landed on this commit exactly there. One of the three corrections (finding R3-1) changed a number that reconciles with the commit's own measurements into one that does not, and applied it to only one of the two places the identical sentence appears, so the commit now contradicts itself in the very sentence it set out to fix. The second (finding R3-2) replaced an unsupported sensitivity claim with a differently unsupported one. That is two new minors bought with a round convened to clear three. The right shape would have been: harden the sampler only, leave the three prose minors in the commit body per rule 11 and harvest them at the M3 boundary per rule 13. Calling this over-polishing would be too harsh on the hardening and too kind on the prose; the accurate statement is that the round was earned by one of its four items and diluted by the other three.

verified: Staged diff hashes to 57ddc63d... as stated; git diff --cached --name-only contains no src/main/ path -- three files, all docs/build/test.

Round-2 approved bytes recovered from the r2 packet and diffed against the staged file: http/build.gradle.kts is IDENTICAL between the two rounds (the java.io.tmpdir fix, the 20-minute task timeout, the test-task exclude and the JaCoCo disable are untouched), and the only backlog delta is the 152->166 word and the appended hardening paragraph (the M0.52 row is unchanged).

In the test file the delta is confined to: the samplerFailures declaration, the retry loop inside the sample Runnable, the try/catch(Throwable) around the sampler loop, the two new post-join assertions, and the two comment blocks at 355-360 and 366-370. The per-window cadence loop, the 2.0 threshold, the loadSamples filter, the hasSizeGreaterThan(10) guard, the warm-up probe and its 2000ms bound, the peak-heap bound and the 10x/128 MiB ratio loop are byte-identical to the round-2 approved text.

The hardening actually closes the hole. countFiles can only fail with an Exception, which the retry records and returns on; anything else (an Error under -Xmx256m, for instance) escapes the retry and is caught by the outer catch(Throwable). samples cannot be empty when samplerFailures is empty, so the samples.get(size-1) at line 323 cannot throw before the isEmpty() assertion above it has already failed. The final sample.run() after the loop guarantees a fresh timestamp, so the 5s bound is a real check and not a tautology, and it is not tight enough to flake (worst case ~1s of sleep plus one forced GC).

Comment claims re-derived rather than taken on trust: 24 x ~223 KB = ~5.1 MiB against 8 MiB is ~0.64 (javadoc says ~0.65, ok); a 0.62 true ratio puts the (0.4, 0.9) band at ~16-34 producers (ok); 4.33 files/s x 10s = ~43 and 16 files/s x 10s = ~160 (ok, and this is the round-2 minor correctly fixed); 2.0/0.792 = 2.53x above the ceiling max and 4.33/2.0 = 2.17x below the floor regime (ok); 0.790 files/s x 5s = 3.95 files per flush, matching 'one 4-file flush per ceiling interval' (ok); SegmentPublisher issues one store.put and DefaultIngest's log.commit issues a second, so 'two objects per flush (segment + delta)', each with LocalFsBinStore's .v sidecar, is 4 files (ok); the Gradle task's 20-minute timeout is wider than the test's own 900s @Timeout, so JUnit fires first and names the test (ok).

Cost lens: no production code and therefore no change to any object-store request rate. The test's own instrumentation walks a local temp directory once per second -- per-second and per-segment, not per record, shard, partition or index -- and it is a filesystem walk in a test fixture, not a LIST against a store, so cost.md R2/R3 are not engaged. Finding R3-3 is about instrument choice, not about a rate.
notes: Style nits, filed here rather than as findings because neither has a failure scenario (review.md rule 6): the first line of the new comment block at line 223 is indented four spaces deeper than its own continuation lines, an artefact of the round-3 edit; and moving countFiles into the sample Runnable means written.get() is now read AFTER the walk while heap is read before it, where MemoryFlatUnderTenXBodySizeTest reads written first -- so the 10x bound is paired with a slightly later byte count and is fractionally looser. The drift is a few KB of a 128 MiB floor and does not matter.

check-tdd's failure is structural and correctly attributed: tdd_scan maps the class to :http:test by source set, and the class is excluded from that task, so the script runs nothing. The backlog's M0.52 row states this accurately and distinguishes it from the two blind spots AGENTS.md already records. Reported, not re-checked.

Backlog honesty (non-negotiable 4): the row's account of the cap decision is accurate as far as it goes -- it says plainly that the hardening was done past the cap and why, and it does not claim the round was forced. Its one inaccuracy is finding R3-1, which the row itself introduced.
